title: McFlurry IS BACK! First Start Up & Dyno + Carbon Fiber Turbo Inlet

carbon_inlet_build.process: 3D scan of engine bay (Revopoint MetroX scanner with reflective markers and scanning spray) -> CAD -> 3D-printed buck (two pieces, plastic welded) -> bodywork, clear, wet sand 600-1500 grit and buff -> two-piece split mold -> vacuum-bagged resin infusion (held ~28.5 inHg vacuum, leak-checked) -> clear coat -> trim to fit; part made slightly long on purpose for trimming
carbon_inlet_build.notes: Ty had not done carbon work in ~5 years; part very light; replaces stock-style inlet to the turbo; rubber coupler kept at turbo

people.tuning_help: Brett LaLa (caption 'Brett Lola'/'Lala', called 'Coyote god'; said to have the fastest Coyote car)

cars.owner_driver: McFarland Racing (Cleetus driving on dyno; 'Steve' asked to drive next track outing, low confidence)

base_vehicle.model: Mustang Fox body (said 'not a fox body' as a joke about power)

engine.notes: same engine as before the turbo change ('it's the same engine')
engine.valve_covers: Motion Raceworks billet valve covers, black, very thin

power_adder.turbo_desc: class-legal 76 mm 'maxed out for its size' turbo; caption reads 'Ultra street 76 mm with T5 inlet VMAN discharge 139 AR' -> likely Ultra Street-class 76 mm, V-band discharge, 1.39 A/R turbine housing (inlet flange 'T5' as captioned, low confidence); brand not clearly stated; called the most expensive turbo ever in the shop; heavier than their 98 mm
power_adder.class_note: 76 mm is the class limit; competitors all run similarly extreme 76 mm turbos
power_adder.boost_control: CO2 dome pressure; boost cut added after an overboost
power_adder.oil_feed_restrictor: nitrous jet used as restrictor in turbo oil feed to cure decel smoke (Coyote makes high oil pressure)

converter.fact: new converter installed; concern it may be too loose

fuel_system.fact: no longer the 'crazy fuel cell'; fuel level now visible

body.fact: front bumper replaced and braced after previous outing bent it under itself

previous_outing.fact: last time out it 'went 70' (likely a 7.0x pass) and bent the front bumper

dyno.result: unintended overboost; lifted at 5,200 rpm; no number given

dyno.boost_psi: 26 falling to 23 at high rpm (back-pressure suspected)
31 rolling in, 29 at ~8,000 rpm (peak power rpm)

failures.cause: first loaded pull overboosted to 35 psi due to a setting change; boost cut added
smoke on deceleration from excessive oil pressure to turbo; fixed with restrictor

targets.hp: ~1,600 on a good day plus ram air (claim)

cars.confidence: high for dyno numbers; low for turbo brand/flange spec

behaviors: boost falls off at high rpm with flat dome pressure (turbine back-pressure)
turbo oil feed needs restrictor on high-oil-pressure engines
